question: Can a de novo antibody design pipeline targeting intrinsically disordered proteins be validated computationally by AF2-derived confidence?

findings_chain.conclusion: Only interface PAE transfers across independent scaffolds; pLDDT and ipTM do not.
findings_chain.evidence: External 6-scaffold transfer evaluation: PAE median scaffold Spearman 0.70-0.87; pLDDT Spearman ~0 (five head/loss ablations falsified); ipTM insufficient reliable pairs (2/6 scaffolds).

findings_chain.conclusion: Single-sequence AF2 (no MSA) cannot recapitulate a real antibody-peptide binding interface; its low scores are an MSA-absence artifact, not a design failure.
findings_chain.evidence: Native 6YXM crystal complex (ACPA Fab H:L + LPGQGERG): single-sequence interface PAE 27.66, ipTM 0.22, pLDDT 0.18 - classified as non-binding despite being a bound crystal structure.

findings_chain.conclusion: MSA-based AF2 restores the antibody chain's fold confidence but does NOT discriminate native vs scrambled short peptides via ipTM.
findings_chain.evidence: With MSA (colabfold multimer v3, recycle 0): native ipTM 0.753, scrambled peptide ipTM 0.755 - statistically indistinguishable. ipTM is whole-complex and dominated by the 435-residue antibody, so the 8-residue peptide interface carries negligible weight.

findings_chain.conclusion: The only discriminating signal for candidate-interface quality is the local candidate-to-antigen interface PAE, not whole-complex ipTM.
findings_chain.evidence: candidate-to-antigen PAE transfers across scaffolds (Spearman 0.70-0.87) and is the deployment-grade signal; ipTM abstained per the frozen deployment contract.

assets_delivered: V6 general-protein confidence model (ipTM Pearson r=0.950)
PAE single-axis candidate-interface confidence (3-seed, 6-gate deployment contract)
External scaffold calibration methodology (6 independent scaffolds, 3 preregistered discovery rounds, five-axis isolation)
IDP research platform with honest capability manifest (publication/idp_platform_capability_v1.json)
C1 R&D preregistration + H1/H2 experiment scripts + generalized ensemble contact scorer (publication/idp_rd_c1_preregistration.json)
honest_end_state: The computational validation loop is closed: single-sequence AF2 cannot fold the antibody (no MSA), MSA cannot discriminate the short peptide (ipTM is antibody-dominated), and only interface PAE provides a relative ranking signal. The question of whether a de novo designed antibody actually binds a disordered target cannot be answered computationally in this setting.
recommended_next_step: Wet-lab validation (SPR/BLI) of 3-5 designed candidates is the only remaining path to answer the binding question. The PAE single-axis model provides the candidate ranking; wet-lab provides the absolute validation.
claim_boundary: This record documents why AF2-derived whole-complex confidence (ipTM) and single-sequence AF2 are unsuitable for validating short antibody-peptide interfaces. It does not claim antibody design success. No wet-lab validation has been performed.
